clue.text: Parliamentary official who cracks

parts.note: the party official who keeps MPs in line shares a name with the lash that cracks

explanation.surface: A government official is breaking under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracks' looks like breaking down; it is what the lash of the same name does. In Parliament this official enforces party discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit one word: the party enforcer in Parliament and a lash that is cracked.

clue.text: Inflate an account maybe — or unduly reduce one

definitions.meaning: to exaggerate in depicting, as an overblown story told
to take out more money from a bank account than it holds

explanation.surface: Someone either pads a bank statement or drains the account too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Account' is first a story told, then a bank account.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to depict with exaggeration and to withdraw more than the balance of a bank holding.

clue.text: A positive sign

definitions.meaning: an advantage or benefit, a good point

explanation.surface: Something is an encouraging omen.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a benefit and the cross-shaped mathematical symbol for addition.

clue.text: Pull up in pain when learning the hard way

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for pain

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to tow is to pull

explanation.surface: Someone flinches with pain during a tough lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for pull, as a down clue reads upwards; 'in' places that inside the pain word. 'Swot' is British slang for studying hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive, laborious studying, as by a keen student cramming for exams, is learning the hard way.

clue.text: Clinched the deal and shut up

definitions.meaning: to have completed a sale is to have sealed it
fastened or locked, like a shop at night

explanation.surface: A negotiator sealed the agreement and then stopped talking.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both a finalised business sale and a shop or door that has been shut.

clue.text: Perfect demonstration of being impervious to noise

parts.note: sound means whole, in perfect condition
a proof is a demonstration of a truth

explanation.surface: Something is a flawless showing of how to keep sound out.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulated so that no noise can pass through, as a recording studio is.

clue.text: Bill raised sail going out to French port

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are turned to read upwards

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

indicators.note: going out suggests the letters of sail wander off their order

explanation.surface: A boat with a hoisted sail sets off towards a port in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AC into CA; 'going out' rearranges SAIL to LAIS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a ferry harbour on the north coast of France facing Dover.

clue.text: A touching article or tract

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Seems to ask whether a piece is moving or merely a pamphlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a stretch of land, a region or zone.

clue.text: Poor house for a student near part of Brighton actually

indicators.note: near tells us the student letter sits beside the place name

parts.note: Hove is a town joined to Brighton, whose residents famously say they live in 'Hove, actually'
L, from the learner plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: Advice on cheap student digs in a Brighton neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: Hove is a well-to-do town next to Brighton on England's south coast; 'Hove, actually' is a joke about its snobbish residents.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovel is a squalid, mean dwelling, a shack or slum.

clue.text: Be delighted, given small part in broadcast

parts.note: a walk-on is a small part for an actor with no lines
to air a show is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: An actor is thrilled to get a minor role on television.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes elation so great that one seems to float.

clue.text: As parties get boisterous, they need indulgent hosts

indicators.note: boisterous behaviour throws things about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Rowdy parties need generous people to throw them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosts' looks social; it is the biological sense of organisms that feed others.
explanation.definitionFit: Organisms living off another creature depend on a host, as fleas or freeloaders do.

clue.text: Lake in old colony, as Africans changed name to Malawi

definitions.text: Lake in old colony, as Africans changed name to Malawi

indicators.note: in says the lake sits inside the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A history note on how an African lake got its present name.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the clue is true colour: British Nyasaland became Malawi in 1964, and its lake was renamed with it.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the colonial-era name of the great Rift Valley body of water now called Lake Malawi.

clue.text: Swallow one cocktail

parts.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Knock back one mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb about drinking; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin and vermouth drink is a classic mixed cocktail.

clue.text: Means of communication with a walrus?

definitions.meaning: an old word for the walrus, from Lappish

explanation.surface: Asks how one might talk to a walrus.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both that of the telegraphic code and an archaic word for the tusked sea mammal.

clue.text: Hostelry needs plaudits for introduction of something new

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry
an ovation is applause, plaudits

explanation.surface: A pub needs praise for launching something new.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing in new methods or ideas is precisely what a novelty or invention does.

clue.text: Down payment I posted off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone wrong, out of order

explanation.surface: Someone has sent off an advance payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum paid upfront to secure a purchase is a down payment.

clue.text: A temple ornament?

parts.note: worn across the head at the temples, not in a place of worship

explanation.surface: Suggests a decoration in a shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temple' suggests a religious building; it is the side of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled crescent worn on the head sits against the temples, so it ornaments them.

clue.text: A worn out tree

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A tree that is old and exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash is a small tree with red berries, also called this name.

clue.text: Travel to a part of India

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: An instruction to take a trip to India.
explanation.definitionFit: This small coastal state on India's west coast is a former Portuguese colony.

clue.text: Involved in a quest for old things

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so these letters are twisted together

explanation.surface: Someone takes part in a search for old objects.
explanation.definitionFit: Collectible items from the past, such as old furniture, are prized relics.

clue.text: Board has positive answers from two Europeans

parts.note: oui is the French word for yes
ja is the German for yes, the second European's reply

explanation.surface: A committee is agreed by a French and a German member.
explanation.walkthrough: The French and German words for yes give the name of the board used in seances.
explanation.definitionFit: A lettered board used at seances to receive spirit messages.

clue.text: Competitors will be on edge in these arenas

definitions.text: Competitors will be on edge in these arenas

parts.words: Competitors will be on edge in these arenas
parts.note: skaters balance on the edges of their blades, not nervousness

explanation.surface: Tense athletes in the stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on edge' seems to mean nervous; skaters literally ride on blade edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen venues where skaters and hockey players compete are arenas of this kind.

clue.text: Having developed, went around topless

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to have revolved is to have gone around

explanation.surface: Someone grew up and walked about without a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To have grown or changed gradually over time, as species do.

clue.text: Sends for instructions

explanation.surface: Someone sends off for a manual.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb of requesting goods and a plural noun for commands.

clue.text: Sad reflection about everything in Texas city

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
all means everything

explanation.surface: A gloomy musing about everything in Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflection' gives the mirror image DAS, and 'about' wraps it round the word for everything.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a major city in northern Texas, known for oil and its football team.

clue.text: Obtaining material, staff head missed tea break

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word is left out
break means the letters are broken up and reset

explanation.surface: Staff get supplies while their boss skips the tea break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head missed' cuts STAFF to TAFF; 'break' rearranges TEA to ETA.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp lustrous silk or synthetic fabric is a kind of cloth.

clue.text: He is working on a commission

definitions.text: He is working on a commission

parts.words: He is working on a commission
parts.note: a trainee officer works towards an officer's commission, not a paid job

explanation.surface: An artist or salesman busy on a paid assignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commission' suggests a paid job; it is the rank of an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A young trainee in the armed forces hopes to earn a commission as an officer.

clue.text: Wrath possibly shown by head

definitions.meaning: Wrath is a headland at the far north-west of Scotland
a headland jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Someone's anger shows in their face.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape Wrath is the north-western tip of mainland Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A promontory projecting into the sea, such as the one at Wrath, is a headland.

clue.text: Sweet drink on the rocks?

parts.note: liquor is alcoholic drink
a drink on the rocks is served with ice

explanation.surface: A sugary cocktail served over ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A black chewy confection flavoured with a root extract is a kind of sweet or candy.

clue.text: Twice reduced by 50%

parts.note: halve the number of times: two occasions become a single occasion

explanation.surface: A price cut twice by half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by 50%' sounds like a discount; it halves the count of times.
explanation.definitionFit: Half of two occasions is a single occasion, one time only.

clue.text: Take it away from work

parts.note: the idiom 'take it ___' means relax, as one does off duty

explanation.surface: An instruction to carry something home from the office.
explanation.walkthrough: The missing word completes the phrase 'take it ___', meaning to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxed and unhurried, as one is when off duty, completing the phrase about taking things gently.

clue.text: Individual has time to become a VIP

parts.note: a person is an individual
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone takes years to become important.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of rank or importance, a dignitary, is a very important person.

clue.text: King Alfred's spoils?

parts.note: legend says Alfred let some baked goods burn while sheltering with a peasant woman

explanation.surface: Asks what plunder an English king won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoils' looks like war booty; it is what Alfred ruined. In English legend, King Alfred, hiding from the Danes, burnt the baking he was told to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says the king burnt the batch of baked goods he was asked to mind.
